items.body: London-based, Australian-born electronic producer, songwriter and DJ HAAi released her third studio album “DIGITiSE” on October 9 via Mute, on vinyl, CD and digitally. The release arrived alongside a video for “Talking Walls,” a collaboration with producer Skybreak and the Colombian children’s choir Cantoalegre. DIGITiSE by HAAi “DIGITiSE” runs to ten tracks: “RE-HUMANiSE” (feat. Kaiden Ford and ILA), “Printerlude,” “Ignition” (feat. Echonomist), “Depth Perception,” “DIGITiSE” (feat. Pat Alvarez), “Technology,” “HUMANiSE Radio,” “THANK U,” “I Wanna Feel Like Someone” (feat. James Massiah) and “HAAi x Skybreak ‘Talking Walls'” (feat. Cantoalegre). The album follows 2025’s “HUMANiSE,” reusing the same closing choir motif on its opening track, and brings in new collaborators Echonomist and Skybreak alongside returning contributors Pat Alvarez, ILA, James Massiah and Kaiden Ford. HAAi described “DIGITiSE” as “HUMANiSE’s” “bigger, ravey sibling,” adding: “DIGITiSE holds the hand of HUMANiSE and walks it to the club.” ‘Talking Walls’ brings in a children’s choir from Medellín HAAi calls “Talking Walls” “one to hug your mates to at the festival.” Cantoalegre, a children’s choir founded in Medellín, Colombia, in 1984, supplies the vocals alongside Skybreak, the production project of New York and London-raised artist Jack Ramsay. HAAi traces the collaboration to a festival booking in Colombia earlier this year: “I’ve had the fortune of playing in Colombia, and more specifically Medellín, many times. It’s a place I hold very dear to my heart. I was there in January to play a festival and felt the urge to reach out about working with a local kids’ choir. Within two hours of having this thought, I was speaking with the principal of Cantoalegre about what I wanted to do. I’ve worked with different choirs across my last two albums, so it was really exciting to be working with new voices in a city I love so much. There was something about hearing the lyrics through the voices of the next generation that gave the words so much more hope and meaning. It’s an experience I will never forget, and I’m so proud of what we made.” On the album as a whole, HAAi said: “I’ve spent so many hours in clubs – on the dance floor and in the booth – and I really wanted to put that into this new album.” Visuals for the campaign are led by Martin Falck, whose past credits include Fever Ray, The Knife and Icona Pop. DJ dates and an Australian tour with The Avalanches HAAi marks the release with an all-night, open-to-close set at EartH in London on October 31, staged with production and set design by Playbody, and a ten-hour marathon set at Refuge in New York on October 18. She has also announced an Australian tour with The Avalanches for March 2027. Confirmed dates: 9 Oct – Geneva (CH), Electron Festival 10 Oct – Manchester (UK), IPC, b2b with DJ Seinfeld, The Warehouse Project 16 Oct – San Francisco, CA (US), Dom Dolla support b2b DJ Seinfeld at Cow Palace 17 Oct – Miami, FL (US), iiiPoints Festival 18 Oct – New York, NY (US), Open to Close, Refuge 22 Oct – Manchester (UK), 20 Years of the Warehouse Project 23 Oct – Amsterdam (NL), b2b Adiel, Audio Obscura x Raw Factory 24 Oct – Galway (IE), Heineken Greenlight 25 Oct – Athens (GR), b2b Romy, Eden 31 Oct – London (UK), HAAi All Night at EartH 20 Nov – Brighton (UK), Concorde 2 21 Nov – Manchester (UK), Depot Mayfield 27 Nov – Los Angeles, CA (US), Time Warp 28 Nov – San Francisco, CA (US), The Great Northern 3 Dec – Miami (US), b2b Salute, Raw Cuts, The Ground 18 Dec – Bristol (UK), b2b Special Request, Mastery x Glade at Prospect 15 Jan 2027 – Johannesburg (ZA), Fabric at Truth Club 16 Jan 2027 – Cape Town (ZA), Castle of Good Hope 19 Feb 2027 – Paris (FR), Polari at FVTVR 5 March 2027 – Melbourne (AU), Royal Botanic Gardens, with The Avalanches 6 March 2027 – Brisbane (AU), On The Banks, with The Avalanches 7 March 2027 – Sydney (AU), Sydney Opera House, with The Avalanches About HAAi HAAi is the stage name of Teneil Throssell, a producer, songwriter and DJ who grew up in Karratha, Western Australia, before moving to the UK to play guitar in the psychedelic rock duo Dark Bells. She began DJing after that band split and held a two-year residency at the London club Phonox from late 2016. Her debut EP, “Systems Up, Windows Down,” came out on Mute on November 14, 2019. The label released her debut album, “Baby, We’re Ascending,” on May 27, 2022, with guests including Jon Hopkins; Pitchfork wrote that the record was “something bigger, something that transcends the club without turning its back on it.” In 2023, HAAi compiled an edition of the “DJ-Kicks” series for !K7 and released “Lights Out,” a collaboration with Fred again.. and Romy. Her second album, “HUMANiSE,” followed on Mute on October 10, 2025, preceded by the singles “Can’t Stand To Lose,” “Shapeshift” (with KAM-BU), “Satellite,” “Hey!” and “Stitches.” The album was named to the year-end lists of Rough Trade, Disco Pogo and Resident, and The Quietus described it as “transcendent.” An accompanying concert film, shot at London’s Drumsheds, featured album collaborators Jon Hopkins, Alexis Taylor, Obi Franky, KAM-BU and TRANS VOICES. “DIGITiSE,” announced in June 2026 and preceded by the singles “Ignition” (feat. Echonomist) and “I Wanna Feel Like Someone” (feat. James Massiah), extends “HUMANiSE’s” themes into a dancefloor-oriented record built from HAAi’s own DJ sets. HAAi was named Beatport’s Artist of the Month over the summer of 2026 and performed a run of shows at London’s Courtyard Theatre and the Royal Albert Hall ahead of the album’s release. “DIGITiSE” is out now on Mute on vinyl, CD and digitally, with HAAi set to tour it through 2026 and into an Australian run with The Avalanches in March 2027.

items.body: Finnish electropunk duo I Think I Broke Something releases the single “Decadence” on 7 October 2026. The track is the third single from the duo’s upcoming EP “Another Escape,” due November 5, and the release will be marked with a show at Semifinal in Helsinki the same day. The band calls “Decadence” one of its most accessible tracks to date: “In our world, Decadence is a fairly straightforward electro-industrial punk track. You could describe it as a collision between Viagra Boys and The Prodigy, while still doing its own weird thing in its own universe. It’s probably one of the most radio-friendly tracks we’ve ever made.” Decadence by I Think I Broke Something “Decadence” follows “Illegal,” released August 6, and “Heads Up,” released September 9, as the third single from “Another Escape” ahead of the EP’s November 5 release. “Decadence” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp and Spotify. About I Think I Broke Something I Think I Broke Something, also known as ITIBS, is a Helsinki-based duo made up of Jouni and Miika, active since 2014. The project debuted with the EP “Superman Sabotage Clan” and has since released three full-length albums, including “Still Not Going To,” announced for an October 26, 2022 release as the duo’s third LP, alongside numerous singles and remixes through various labels. That album cycle included the singles “Astral,” released September 2022, “Corpse,” released April 2023, and “Raw,” released July 2023. ITIBS describes its sound as a distorted electronic hybrid that draws on The Prodigy, 3TEETH and Nine Inch Nails and mixes explosive electronics with metal-heavy weight. The duo lists collaborations with The Prodigy’s Maxim, DJ Hyper and Zardonic. “Decadence,” released October 7, follows “Illegal” and “Heads Up” as the third single from the EP “Another Escape,” due November 5 alongside the band’s release show at Semifinal in Helsinki.

items.body: Town & Towers Records releases Heldautomat‘s new single “Liebe ist endlich” on October 9, 2026. It is the third single from the Dortmund, Germany duo’s debut album “Zwischen den Lichtern”, due October 23 on the same label. “Liebe ist endlich” (“Love is finite”) opens with a slow synthesizer introduction before settling into a synth-pop arrangement, with Christian Purwien’s vocals staying restrained throughout. The refrain states its theme directly: “Liebe ist endlich / Sie ist leider vergänglich” (“Love is finite / Unfortunately, it is transient”). Heldautomat describe the track on Bandcamp as a song with “no metaphors, no way out, no redemption. Just the quiet realisation that things come to an end.” Purwien writes the lyrics and sings. Kowa plays the synthesizers. Olaf Wollschläger produced the single. Club mix and video for ‘Liebe ist endlich’ The digital release also includes a “Videomix” of the duo’s first single, “Am ersten Tag”, and a club mix of “Liebe ist endlich” produced by Purwien & Kowa, Purwien and Kowa’s other recording project. Heldautomat also posted an official video for “Liebe ist endlich” on YouTube. “Liebe ist endlich” is open for digital pre-order on Bandcamp. Liebe ist endlich by Heldautomat About Heldautomat Heldautomat is the Dortmund, Germany duo of Christian Purwien and Thomas Kowa, working with analogue synthesizers, piano and a drum machine alongside Purwien’s vocals. Purwien co-founded Second Decay in Witten in 1987 with Andreas Michael Sippel, after the pair had performed as Blue Velvet from 1985. Second Decay recorded entirely on analogue synthesizers and released albums including “Taste” (1994) and “The Hunt” (1998) before going quiet after 2002. Emmo.Biz Records has since reissued “The Hunt” on green double vinyl and “Taste” on a second double-LP edition. Purwien and Kowa also record together as Purwien & Kowa, a project with five albums behind it and a sixth, “Sechs”, in the works. The duo played the 18th Elektrisch Festival on February 27, 2026, in a set drawn 70 percent from Second Decay material. Heldautomat released its debut single, “Am ersten Tag“, on May 15, 2026. “Anders Sein” followed on August 14, reworking a song Sippel and Purwien wrote for Second Decay’s “Taste” in 1994. “Liebe ist endlich” is the third single, and precedes the October 23 album “Zwischen den Lichtern”, produced throughout by Olaf Wollschläger and including a cover of Nine Inch Nails‘ “Hurt”. A vinyl edition of the album, limited to 100 hand-signed copies, is available alongside the digital release.

items.body: Silence has a talent for passing itself off as peace. Two people can share a room, exchange the necessary pleasantries, and conduct an entire argument without troubling the air between them. Inside, every withheld accusation is already gathering speed. Given enough time, even “How was your day?” can begin to sound like a contact sport. Milan quartet October take that condition onto the ice in their video for Universe. The fourth single from their debut album, Dancing Like an Idiot, out now through Waddafuzz! Records, follows the uncomfortable distance between what a relationship looks like from the outside and what its participants are putting themselves through within it. A frozen surface can conceal considerable commotion, and October have enlisted a hockey team to give those private collisions a public airing. The song itself has a supple, sophisticated swing. A rhythmic bassline brings the new wave funk of Roxy Music and Japan to mind, its firm articulation keeping the groove grounded as sustained guitar tones stretch above it. The snare lands at deliberate intervals, leaving generous space around each strike. There is a progressive streak in the arrangement, a willingness to let the instrumental passages stretch and change shape without losing the underlying rhythm. Gianluca Villa sings in a silky upper register reminiscent of Peter Gabriel, his measured delivery building to increasingly impassioned peaks on the line “A Message from the stars.” A gentle guitar jangle carries the song forward, lifting some of its emotional weight. A string interlude zigzags through the arrangement as the vocal rises into a high croon, and tension builds until the full force of the performance comes crashing back. Directed and edited by Fabrizio Grasso, with concept and production by Davide Debenedetti for Filmico, the video makes that division visible. October perform on the rink beneath bright backlights, framed against rows of empty seats, while members of Sgularat Hockey Club Milano skate around them in yellow and black. The musicians hold their positions as the players accelerate, compete, and cut across the space between them. Pads, helmets, and sticks give anger and frustration a physical vocabulary; the ice supplies the emotional temperature. There is something both funny and painfully apt about bringing protective equipment into a love song. Here, the action surrounding the band becomes the argument nobody is having aloud: misunderstandings, thwarted attempts at connection, and the helplessness of trying to reach someone who has become difficult to recognise. Grasso lets the rink carry the metaphor, its broad white expanse accommodating all that activity without offering much warmth. Watch the video for Universe below: October formed in Milan in 2024, bringing together musicians whose backgrounds include Grandi Animali Marini, Il Fieno, NOA, and Egokid, alongside collaborations with Veracrash and I Ministri. Villa handles guitar and vocals, joined by bassist Dario Giordano, drummer Paolo Soffientini, and synth player Davide “dEbE” Debenedetti. Their debut was recorded at Casamedusa with Francesco Campanozzi and Frigo Studio with Francesco Ferrari, then mixed and mastered by Paolo Mauri. Released on March 30, 2026, Dancing Like an Idiot is available digitally and on vinyl. Listen to Universe below and order the album here. items.body: “Rub’a’Dub Love” is 8-bit digital reggae in the style of the 1980s, and it originally appeared on the album Where My Style Comes From, released in June. On 2 October it came back in two remixes on UK-based digital dub and reggae label Superchip: raggamuffin boom-bap from Hopebullet, a DJ and sound engineer from Osaka who also goes by Ranking Jin, and a second version by RJD. Behind it are deejay Daddy Cookiz and producer Simma, with singer Ponchita Peligros as guest. Simma is Nathan Simm from Hull, England, a producer and DJ who started out in Ableton during the 2020 lockdown, runs Superchip and also records as Polyecho and Square Nath. His 2024 debut, Simma Enters The Game, mixed digital reggae, dubbed-out hip-hop and 8-bit chiptune and drew on the German label Jahtari and the Scottish sound system Mungo’s Hi Fi. Daddy Cookiz has deejayed since 2005 and grew up on Jamaican sound system culture, and he takes his cues from Super Cat, Yellowman and Shabba Ranks. items.body: German darkwave artist Die Tödin releases a self-titled compilation on 30 October through Heartworm Press, the label founded by Cold Cave’s Wesley Eisold. The collection gathers nine recordings made between 2022 and 2025 and expands on Die Tödin’s earlier “Selected Singles” release on Minimalkombinat. Die Tödin said the compilation follows a difficult stretch of her life: “The last two years have been very difficult for me, so I want to draw a symbolic line under that period with this release.” She described the collection as a near-complete retrospective, calling it “almost everything Die Tödin has released to date.” Die Tödin’s self-titled compilation on Heartworm Press The release comes on white vinyl and on a Black Static vinyl edition limited to 200 copies. Both pressings include an 11-by-17-inch newsprint poster. The tracklist: Ich bin schon tot Angepasste Spießerschweine Wild Gift living that DSBM life Dissonanz des Lebens Im Schatten Verderben La Bruja / Die Geister, die ich rief Verderben by Die Tödin About Die Tödin Die Tödin records as a darkwave artist based in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. Her back catalogue includes the “Selected Singles” release on Minimalkombinat, drawn together with other tracks from 2022 to 2025 into the self-titled compilation due 30 October on Cold Cave member Wesley Eisold’s Heartworm Press. The compilation, pressed on white and limited Black Static vinyl, becomes Die Tödin’s most complete release to date.

Side-Line previously covered the project’s 2023 single “I Want More,” and in 2025 XTR Human contributed a remix to Massive Ego‘s single “Hit the Kerb Running.” Stabel’s catalogue under the XTR Human name includes the albums “G.O.L.D” (2021) and “Schrank” (2024), followed by the “Rave God” EP earlier in 2026, with a remix by Houses of Heaven. Wie Ein Gott Records launched in Berlin in 2022 with the compilation “VA#01.” “Fake” is XTR Human’s first release on the label and opens a new release series there.

items.excerpt: コルトレーンの歌心は、どこから来たのか フランスのラジオ局フランス・ミュージックが、サックス奏者で研究者でもあるラファエル・アンベール（Raphaël Imbert）へのインタビューを公開した。テーマは、ジョン・コルトレーンがどのように独自のスタイルを築いたかである。   アンベールは、少年期の家族や宗教的な背景に、コルトレーンの歌唱性の源を見るという。そこにブルースとR&Bの影響が重なり、さらに、１日10時間に及んだとされる練習を支えた理論への貪欲さが加わる。30歳前後で知られるようになってからの約10年で、音楽史と思想に影響を与えた存在として語られている。 宗教的な背景、ブルース、R&B。ジャズの周辺にあった複数の水脈が、一人の奏者のなかでどう合流したのか。この対話は、その過程を順に辿る試みだと思える。コルトレーンの音源を聴き返すときの、一本の補助線になるだろう。 出典：https://www.radiofrance.fr/francemusique/comment-john-coltrane-a-t-il-developpe-son-style-unique-entre
items.body: コルトレーンの歌心は、どこから来たのか フランスのラジオ局フランス・ミュージックが、サックス奏者で研究者でもあるラファエル・アンベール（Raphaël Imbert）へのインタビューを公開した。テーマは、ジョン・コルトレーンがどのように独自のスタイルを築いたかである。   アンベールは、少年期の家族や宗教的な背景に、コルトレーンの歌唱性の源を見るという。そこにブルースとR&Bの影響が重なり、さらに、１日10時間に及んだとされる練習を支えた理論への貪欲さが加わる。30歳前後で知られるようになってからの約10年で、音楽史と思想に影響を与えた存在として語られている。 宗教的な背景、ブルース、R&B。ジャズの周辺にあった複数の水脈が、一人の奏者のなかでどう合流したのか。この対話は、その過程を順に辿る試みだと思える。コルトレーンの音源を聴き返すときの、一本の補助線になるだろう。 出典：https://www.radiofrance.fr/francemusique/comment-john-coltrane-a-t-il-developpe-son-style-unique-entretien-avec-raphael-imbert-6339331 20年を超える二人の『Nearness』 前出のラジオ局、フランス・ミュージックよりもう一本。ジャズ・ボーカリストのリズ・ライト（Lizz Wright）と、ピアニストのケニー・バンクスSr.（Kenny Banks Sr.）が初めて完全にデュオに徹して作ったアルバム『Nearness』について採り上げている。 ふたりの出会いは大学時代のアトランタ。以来20年以上、共同作業を重ねてきたという。収録されているのは、スピリチュアル、ジャズ・スタンダード、オリジナル曲。バンクスはピアノとオルガンを担当し、プロデューサーはChris Bruce、最終曲はア・カペラである。出典によれば、二人が教会で共に歩んだことと、ジャズ、R&B、即興への関心が、この作品の土台になっている。   教会という共通の場と、ジャズ・R&B・即興への関心。二つの水脈が長い協働のなかで重なってきたことが、スピリチュアルとスタンダードを一枚に並べる構成に表れているように思える。ピアノとオルガン、そして最後は声だけ。編成を絞った作りが、題名の「近さ」にそのまま重なる。 出典：https://www.radiofrance.fr/francemusique/podcasts/au-coeur-du-jazz/lizz-wright-intime-proximite-1727454 旅の混乱が題になった─ クリス・デイヴィス・トリオ『Lost in Geneva』 ピアニストのクリス・デイヴィス（Kris Davis）が、ロバート・ハースト、ジョナサン・ブレイクとのトリオで、新作『Lost in Geneva』をリリースした。アルバムのタイトルは、旅のアクシデントの逸話に由来するという。 表題曲は、時差ぼけと不慣れな環境による混乱を喚起する曲である。2024年の『Run the Gauntlet』以来、3人は数えきれない時間を路上とステージで共にしてきた。 ピアノ・トリオは、三者の対話で成り立つ形式である。時間と場所を共有した経験の厚みが、題名や表題曲という形で作品に刻まれている。『Run the Gauntlet』から続く道中の記録として、並べて聴けるだろう。 出典：https://www.radiofrance.fr/francemusique/podcasts/au-coeur-du-jazz/kris-davis-trio-complicite-amplifiee-par-la-desorientation-6244148 クリス・デイヴ、モノネオン、ジャスタス・ウェスト─11月、ビルボードライブ横浜・東京・大阪で ドラマーのクリス・デイヴ（Chris Dave）、ベーシストのモノネオン（MonoNeon）、ギタリストのジャスタス・ウェスト（Justus West）が、11月にビルボードライブの横浜・東京・大阪で公演を行う。 日程は11月17日が横浜、19日が東京、20日が大阪で、各日2ステージ（開演17:30・20:30）。告知文はこの公演を「ジャンルの境界を軽やかに越えた予測不能のセッション」と紹介。ドラム、ベース、ギターという三つの楽器の奏者が、三つの街で同じ顔ぶれの音を交わす。 出典：https://www.billboard-live.com/tokyo/show?event_id=ev-21707 ミシェル・ンデゲオチェロ『Synonym』─他人の歌を読み替える 英ガーディアン紙が、ミシェル・ンデゲオチェロ（Meshell Ndegeocello）の新作『Synonym』のレビューを掲載した。見出しは、ボブ・ディランからJ-Loまでの鮮やかなオールスターによる再解釈（原題：vivid all-star reinventions）。 レビューが具体的に挙げているのは、たとえば次のような例である。Cat Powerとの「Don’t You Want Me」はレゲエに作り替えられ、Callahanとの「With God on Our Side」が収められている。Anohniとの「I Got You Babe」は、音数を絞ったジャズ・アレンジ（原文：sparse jazz）になっている。さらにグラスパー（Glasper）の参加にも触れられている。 ジャズは、他ジャンルの曲を取り込み、自分たちの言葉で語り直すことを繰り返してきた。本作もまた、その伝統の延長に置いて聴くことができるだろう。 出典：https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/oct/01/meshell-ndegeocello-synonym-review-vivid-all-star-reinventions-of-everyone-from-bob-dylan-to-j-lo オスカー・ブラウン・ジュニア生誕100年、その遺産を語る 英国のジャズ情報サイトUK Jazz Newsが、シンガーのアンバー・ウィークス（Amber Weekes）へのインタビュー「Oscar Brown, Jr. – Centenary Interview」を掲載した。 ジャズ・ボーカリストで作曲家のオスカー・ブラウン・ジュニアの生誕100年を記念する企画で、ブラウンの芸術的な遺産と影響が語られている。歌い手であり作曲家でもあった人物の仕事を、同じ歌い手が語る。節目の年にその名前に触れることは、残された作品を聴き直す入口にもなる。 出典：https://ukjazznews.com/oscar-brown-jr-centenary-interview-with-amber-weekes アルダーナとルバルカバ、タイニー・デスクで 米NPRの企画「Tiny Desk Concert」に、サックス奏者のメリッサ・アルダーナ（Melissa Aldana）が、キューバのピアニスト、ゴンサロ・ルバルカバ（Gonzalo Rubalcaba）とともに登場した。2026年9月29日付で公開された映像である。   ルバルカバがキューバ出身のピアニストであることから、この共演にはキューバの音楽とジャズの往来という文脈が重なると思える。机ひとつの小さな空間を舞台にした企画に、キューバ出身のピアニストを迎えた一本が加わった。 出典：https://www.npr.org/2026/09/29/g-s1-141836/melissa-aldana-gonzalo-rubalcaba-tiny-desk-concert 今週すでにお伝えしたニュース ジャズは“間違えてから”が面白い─創立70年「飯田ジャズスクール」で学ぶ【ジャムセッション講座 第41回】 三宅純が手がけたウクライナ映画『Oxygen Station』オリジナル・サウンドトラックが配信リリース ラルフ・ハイデル、山本達久 、Tatsuro Murakami によるライブ “the session”開催 投稿 【ARBAN WEEKLY｜今週の話題まとめ】コルトレーンの歌心を分析／オスカー・ブラウン・ジュニアの遺産／リズ・ライトとケニー・バンクスSr.の新作 ほか は ARBAN に最初に表示されました。

items.body: Israeli gothic metal band Fatum Aeternum has rebuilt “P.W.Y.P.” for a streaming release, bringing the track back from their 2012 EP “The Sermon.” The self-released single went out digitally on 25 September 2026. The new version keeps the original ’80s glam-rooted guitar riff while adding aggressive male vocals, a female counter voice, cello and a full gospel choir. Where the 2012 recording leaned on social commentary, the rebuilt arrangement expands it into a more layered, theatrical gothic sound the band describes as a dark sermon. “P.W.Y.P.” is the second single in Fatum Aeternum’s renewed run of releases, following the comeback single “As Above, So Below” on 25 August 2026. That single introduced a new six-piece lineup – Steve Gershin, Evelyn Shor Gershin, Dr. Joe, Victor Grassiano, Max Datskovsky and Mark Muzykant – which also plays on “P.W.Y.P.” The track was recorded at Lodge Studios in Northampton, UK. Denis Saenko handled mixing and mastering, with additional mixing by Gershin; Tayo Olawepo arranged and recorded the choir. The band’s promotional materials cite Lacrimosa, Therion and Haggard as reference points. “P.W.Y.P.” is available to stream on Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, Amazon Music, Deezer and SoundCloud. About Fatum Aeternum Fatum Aeternum formed in Tel Aviv, Israel, in 2006, built around Steve Gershin on mandolin, bass and vocals, alongside Ze’ev Gut on fiddle and vocals and Olga Braverman on flute and vocals. The group’s first full lineup added Ilya Surnin on drums, Dan Yoffe on guitar and Rivka Aizenberg on viola, playing a self-described “renaissance metal” blend of folk and metal. Braverman left in 2007 and Gut in 2008, staying on as a guest musician as the band shifted toward a heavier, more electrified sound. Gershin considered disbanding the group in 2009 and recorded a memorial album of earlier material instead; Evelyn Shor Gershin joined permanently around the same time, stabilising the lineup. The band re-recorded its debut album “This Dream Is Dead” several times before releasing it on CD in 2011. On 24 September 2011, Fatum Aeternum played the 12th Children of the Night Gothic Festival in Kyiv, Ukraine, its first show outside Israel, sharing the bill with Waves Under Water and Diary of Dreams. The video for “Apocalypse Now” followed on YouTube in April 2012 and aired on MTV Israel’s “Headbangers Ball” that June. The band self-released the EP “The Sermon” in September 2012, recorded at Lodge Studios in Northampton, UK, and opened for Apoptygma Berzerk the same month before going on hiatus in 2013. Gershin and Evelyn Shor Gershin rebuilt the lineup with George Falk and Igor May in 2014, releasing the single “One Bastard” that April and the maxi-single “The Pain” later the same year. The EP “The Darkest Hour” followed in 2015, then “Mass Suicide of Human Race” in 2017 and “Singing Songs of Desperation” in 2020. Fatum Aeternum returned in 2026 after a three-year gap, a pause the band’s own site attributes to health issues within the group. The comeback single “As Above, So Below” arrived on 25 August 2026 with a new six-piece lineup of Gershin, Evelyn Shor Gershin, Dr. Joe, Victor Grassiano, Max Datskovsky and Mark Muzykant. “P.W.Y.P.,” a rebuilt version of the 2012 “The Sermon” track, follows as the second single in that renewed run.

items.body: David J, a co-founder, bassist and co-songwriter of the post-punk bands Bauhaus and Love and Rockets, releases the single “Requiem for the Rose Garden” on 51 Recordings on 8 October 2026. The song is a protest aimed at the Trump administration, built around the White House Rose Garden as a target that is both symbolic and literal. It is the first track confirmed from J’s new album “Postcards from the Afterlife,” due 27 November on double LP, CD and digital formats. David J on ‘Requiem for the Rose Garden’ J points to physical changes made at the White House since Donald Trump’s first term in office when he explains the song. “It’s basically a protest about Trump’s administration and the atrocities it has visited upon the USA,” he said. “In the context of the song, the Rose Garden at the White House can be seen as a symbolic metaphor, although it is also quite literal. I actually wrote it during Trump’s first term in office when he had that beautiful garden hacked up. Now, even more horror has been inflicted on it of course, and the elegant East Wing of the building completely decimated which is also highly symbolic.” The backing band on the track is Duende, a Detroit-based group J has worked with extensively in the past. “Requiem for the Rose Garden” streams on Spotify, Apple Music, Tidal, Deezer and Pandora via davidjhaskins.com. ‘Postcards from the Afterlife’ due in November on 51 Recordings “Postcards from the Afterlife” is a 14-song album featuring a revolving cast of musicians and numerous autobiographical references. J sums up its themes as circling the same idea from several angles: “essentially about the poignant persistence of connection, be it in life or in death. Schisms and transitions. Love found and love lost. Requiems, reflection and revelation.” Several tracks carry string arrangements, including a finale recorded with members of the Prague Symphony and Philharmonic Orchestras. The rest of the album moves between soulful material, hazy 1960s orchestral pop, European-style chanson and the alternative rock territory J is best known for. “Postcards from the Afterlife” is released on double LP, CD and digital on 27 November. Tour dates for David J David J tours the UK through December 2026, with additional shows in Portugal, Germany and Greece around the “Postcards from the Afterlife” release. 27 November – Porto, Portugal 28 November – Lisbon, Portugal 1 December – London, UK – Moth Club 2 December – Reading, UK – Face Bar 4 December – Hebden Bridge, UK – Trades Club 5 December – Liverpool, UK – Rough Trade 8 December – Edinburgh, UK – The Voodoo Rooms 9 December – Glasgow, UK – Stereo 10 December – Newcastle, UK – The Cluny 11 December – Birmingham, UK – Hare & Hounds 13 December – Brighton, UK – Daltons 15 December – Athens, Greece – Death Disco 17 December – Berlin, Germany – Frannz Club About David J David J, born David John Haskins on 24 April 1957 in Northampton, England, co-founded Bauhaus in 1978, playing bass and co-writing songs including the group’s debut single, “Bela Lugosi’s Dead.” He sang lead vocals on “Who Killed Mr Moonlight?” Bauhaus split in 1983 and has reformed periodically since. Before Love and Rockets, J spent two years as bassist and co-producer for The Jazz Butcher, led by Pat Fish, working on the albums “A Scandal in Bohemia” (1984) and “Sex and Travel” (1985). He formed Love and Rockets in 1985 with fellow former Bauhaus members Daniel Ash and his younger brother Kevin Haskins, playing bass and sharing vocals and songwriting across seven albums released between 1985 and 1998. Both bands have reformed at intervals since their original breakups. J maintained a solo career alongside both bands. He released “Etiquette of Violence” in 1983, “Crocodile Tears and the Velvet Cosh” in 1985 and the singles compilation “On Glass” in 1986. His 1990 album “Songs from Another Season” produced the single “I’ll Be Your Chauffeur,” which reached number one on the Modern Rock Tracks chart. “Urban Urbane” followed in 1992, then “Estranged” in 2003, “Not Long for This World” in 2011 and “An Eclipse of Ships” in 2014. His memoir, “Who Killed Mister Moonlight? (Bauhaus, Black Magick and Benediction),” was published by Jawbone Press in 2014. In 2019 J released the double LP “Missive to an Angel From the Halls of Infamy and Allure.” Side-Line covered the album’s single “I Only Hear Silence Now,” featuring Emily Jane White, alongside a run of 2020 tour dates that included Bauhaus shows at Primavera Sound and Release Athens Festival. “What The Patrons Heard,” a ten-track set of originals and covers recorded over 34 years and first issued to Patreon subscribers, followed on CD and digital on 25 March 2022, with a limited numbered vinyl edition. J’s triple album of archival demos, “Tracks from the Attic,” was announced in February 2024 and released that year. He self-released the spoken-word album “The Mother Tree,” recorded with the band RAQIA, on 6 June 2025. He returned to the “Tracks from the Attic” material in March 2026 with a companion album, “Tracks From the Attic Revisited,” which Side-Line discussed with him the following month in the interview “David J Opens the Attic.” This month’s single and the album that follows continue that run of archival and new recordings.

The night is billed as “The Hotel presents…” and also features Rocheman and performance artist Finn Kennedy. Doors are at 7:30pm, with tickets priced from £13 for Café OTO members up to £20 on the door, available through the venue. The show is The Hotel’s third evening at Café OTO in 2026. Gilbert’s set previews a new album due from The Hotel later this year. Test pressings of the as-yet-unannounced record will be sold at the merch table. Finn Kennedy premieres a newly commissioned piece titled “Streams.” Rocheman closes the night with a full band set, performing as a quartet with Fred Lomas on lead guitar, Tom Powell on drums and Tom Wright on keyboards. Rocheman’s second album, “Basin,” was released on vinyl by The Hotel earlier in 2026, following the EPs “Angel Storm” and “Virtua Saint” on Mindseyerecords.xyz. The self-directed feature film “Taurus,” due in 2027, is among the artist’s forthcoming work. Tickets for The Hotel at Café OTO Tickets cost £13 for Café OTO members, £17 in advance and £20 on the door, available through the venue’s event page. About Bruce Gilbert Bruce Gilbert, born Bruce Clifford Gilbert on 18 May 1946 in Watford, England, co-founded Wire in London in 1976 alongside Colin Newman, Graham Lewis and Robert Gotobed, playing guitar in the band until he left in 2004, following the release of the album “Send.” After Wire’s first breakup in 1980, Gilbert formed a series of projects with bassist Graham Lewis, including Cupol, Dome, P’o and Duet Emmo. Side-Line covered the 2022 remastered reissue of Duet Emmo’s sole album, “Or So It Seems,” Gilbert’s trio recording with Lewis and Daniel Miller. Gilbert also worked with A.C. Marias, producing the single “Drop/So” in 1980 for the group’s Dome label and co-producing the 1989 album “One of Our Girls (Has Gone Missing),” sharing songwriting credit with Angela Conway. Gilbert’s solo albums include “This Way” (1984), “The Shivering Man” (1987) and “Ab Ovo” (1996), all released on Mute, followed by “Ordier” (2004), “Oblivio Agitatum” (2009, Editions Mego) and “Diluvial” (2013, Touch), a collaboration with BAW. He also performs as a DJ under the name DJ Beekeeper. Wire continued without Gilbert after his departure, releasing the mini-album “Nocturnal Koreans” in 2016. Gilbert now appears at Café OTO as part of The Hotel’s third London show of 2026, ahead of a new album the label is set to release later this year.

items.body: German-Finnish futurepop duo PLATRONiC will release the three-track EP “The Emperor’s New Clothes” on 16 October 2026, with three new takes on their March single “Fortress of Fools.” The song started with a poem written by Kay Burden, inspired by Hans Christian Andersen’s “The Emperor’s New Clothes.” Kay originally had a storytelling ballad in mind. Then Sami Jumppanen presented her with a considerably more danceable instrumental, and “Fortress of Fools” became something else entirely. PLATRONiC build three new versions of ‘Fortress of Fools’ For the new EP, they have gone back to the song and, appropriately enough, given it three new “dresses.” The first, “The Dark Electro Country Dress,” is a collaboration with On Moral Ends, the Linköping-based electronic project of Swedish songwriter, singer and multi-instrumentalist Andreas Svensson. His work moves through different electronic and alternative styles, making the collaboration a rather unusual match for PLATRONiC’s futurepop side. For “The Synthpop Mashup Dress,” PLATRONiC worked with Finnish keyboardist, producer and remixer Imppu from Lahti. His work stretches from danceable synthpop to more cinematic electronic sounds, and he has also created remixes and reworks for former Kraftwerk member Wolfgang Flür. The third version stays with Kay and Sami themselves: “The Dark Medieval Gothic Dress.” According to PLATRONiC, “Fortress of Fools” spent several weeks in the Top 10 of both the Klangwald Charts and GEWC following its release earlier this year. The track reached #8 in the Klangwald Charts. The video for “Fortress of Fools” was filmed in Savonlinna, Finland, and Alicante, Spain, and was created and produced by PLATRONiC. PLATRONiC formed in 2020 and consists of German singer-songwriter and co-producer Kay Burden and Finnish composer and producer Sami Jumppanen. Side-Line readers may also know the duo from “How To Ride The Wave,” which appeared earlier this year on Side-Line’s The Freya Files Ukraine benefit compilation. “The Emperor’s New Clothes” tracklist: 1. “Fortress of Fools – The Dark Electro Country Dress” (PLATRONiC & On Moral Ends) 2. “Fortress of Fools – The Synthpop Mashup Dress” (PLATRONiC & Imppu) 3. “Fortress of Fools – The Dark Medieval Gothic Dress” (PLATRONiC) Before the three new “dresses” arrive, “Fortress of Fools” already has its own visual counterpart. “The Emperor’s New Clothes” is available to pre-save via DistroKid ahead of its 16 October release. About PLATRONiC PLATRONiC released the single “Now!” in June 2022, followed by the EP “The Healing” in April 2023 and a cover of Depeche Mode’s “The Things You Said” that August. A reworked version of their debut single “Pride” followed in June 2024, then the winter single “Winter Stores” that December. In March 2025, they released the teaser video for “How to Ride the Wave,” and in December 2025 contributed a cover of Depeche Mode’s “But Not Tonight” to the “In Your Memory 2” tribute compilation. “Fortress of Fools” followed in March 2026 as the duo’s most recent original single, ahead of “The Emperor’s New Clothes” EP arriving on 16 October.

items.body: Town & Towers Records releases Purwien & Kowa‘s new single “Italo-disco in San Francisco” on 9 October 2026, ahead of the German synth-pop duo’s sixth studio album, “Sechs,” due 23 October on the same label. The digital single carries four tracks: German and English versions of “Italo-disco in San Francisco,” an extended “Irgendwas ist immer (12″ Mix)” and a combined “German English Mashup 12″ mix” of the title track. Both language versions of the lyrics string together a run of 1980s references, naming figures including Lady Diana, Mikhail Gorbachev, Blondie, Phil Collins, Falco and Michael Jackson alongside songs such as “Blue Monday,” “Tainted Love,” “Like a Virgin,” “Take On Me,” “99 Luftballons,” “Forever Young” and “The Final Countdown.” “Italo-disco in San Francisco” mixes Italo disco, synthpop, New Wave and EBM, and follows the singles “Concorde” and “Hinter Glas” as the third preview of “Sechs.” Italo-disco in San Francisco by Purwien & Kowa About Purwien & Kowa Purwien & Kowa is a German synth-pop duo based in Dortmund formed by Christian Purwien and Thomas Kowa. Purwien co-founded the electronic/darkwave act Second Decay in 1987, initially under the name Blue Velvet, together with Andreas Michael Sippel. Second Decay released the tape “Monochromes” in 1988 and the 12-inch “Killing Desire” in 1989, followed by “La Décadence Électronique” on CD in 1992, the “Hinter Glas” maxi-CD in 1993 and the album “Taste” in 1994. The band continued with “Der Nerv” in 1995, “Familiar” in 1997, “The Hunt” and “De Luxe” in 1998, “Hotels” in 1999 and “Kaltes, weißes Licht” in 2001, before pausing new material after the 2002 live release “Zwischenfall 1999.” Thomas Kowa, born Thomas Kowalzik in 1969 in Ludwigshafen am Rhein, joined the German synth-pop band No Comment in 1989 and has lived in Switzerland since 2007. He founded the label Nanopop in 2001, closing it in 2007 to focus on writing. Since 2012 he has published a series of crime novels and thrillers. His other current music projects include Nine Seconds and Emily Kinski’s dead. Purwien and Kowa began recording together as Purwien & Kowa, releasing the three-EP digital set “Drei” via Zwei Records in October 2018. The duo also co-hosts the Disko 80 podcast, which covers 1980s music and has featured more than 100 episodes with guests including Joachim Witt, Bernhard Lloyd of Alphaville and Marcus Meyn of Camouflage. Kowa separately co-hosts the “Krimi Schweiz” podcast on Swiss crime fiction. Purwien and Kowa also record together as Heldautomat, whose own single “Liebe ist endlich” reached Town & Towers Records on the same day as “Italo-disco in San Francisco.” The duo performed at the 18th Elektrisch Festival in 2026. Purwien & Kowa returned this year with the singles “Concorde,” “Hinter Glas” and “Italo-disco in San Francisco,” ahead of their sixth studio album, “Sechs,” produced by Olaf Wollschläger and due 23 October 2026 via Town & Towers Records.

items.body: Front Line Assembly’s “Epitaph” turns 25 this year. Metropolis Records released the electro-industrial and EBM album on 8 October 2001, the eleventh full-length studio album by the Vancouver band led by Bill Leeb and Chris Peterson. The record marked Front Line Assembly‘s return to Metropolis Records after the band left the label in October 1999. “Epitaph” runs ten tracks and 54:57, recorded at Cryogenic Studio and produced by Leeb and Peterson. Greg Reely handled mixing and engineering, Brian Gardner mastered the album, and Dave McKean supplied the artwork and design. The tracklist runs “Haloed”, “Dead Planet”, “Backlash”, “Epitaph”, “Everything Must Perish”, “Conscience”, “Decoy”, “Insolence”, “Krank It Up” and “Existance”, the last of which folds in the hidden track “Submerged” after a minute of silence. Metropolis also issued a digipak edition limited to 25,000 copies carrying that bonus track. “Everything Must Perish”, released 11 September 2001, was the only single taken from the album. Bill Leeb told Side-Line at the time that “Epitaph” broke with the band’s earlier reliance on film dialogue samples: “This is the first time we quit using movie samples.” He added: “Sampling is an artform which was criticised in the beginning, but now it’s a respected artform with big money in it. It’s a big business where I don’t feel at ease any longer.” Artoffact Records re-released ‘Epitaph’ on limited edition vinyl in 2015. About Front Line Assembly Bill Leeb founded Front Line Assembly in Vancouver, British Columbia, in 1986 after leaving Skinny Puppy, where he had performed under the stage name Wilhelm Schroeder. Rhys Fulber worked with Leeb from the same period as an early, unofficial collaborator, and Michael Balch became an official member on keyboards and programming in 1988. The band’s debut album, “The Initial Command”, came out on the Belgian label KK at the end of 1987, followed by “State of Mind” on the German label Dossier in January 1988 and “Corrosion” the same year, licensed to Wax Trax! for North America. Balch left after the Gashed Senses & Crossfire tour in 1989 to join Ministry and Revolting Cocks, and Fulber stepped in as an official member. “Gashed Senses & Crossfire” (1989) gave the band its first chart entry, with “Digital Tension Dementia” reaching No. 45 on Billboard’s Hot Dance Club Songs. “Caustic Grip” followed in 1990, the album that began Front Line Assembly’s long-running partnership with mixer and engineer Greg Reely and introduced more guitar-driven material. Chris Peterson debuted as a live percussionist on the accompanying tour before later becoming a full-time member. “Tactical Neural Implant” (1992) brought a more melodic, sample-heavy direction, and “Millennium” (1994) became the band’s first industrial metal record, featuring session guitar from Devin Townsend, who also played on “Hard Wired” (1995). Fulber left in 1997 to concentrate on producing Fear Factory, and Peterson took over his role as the band moved toward the electronica and big-beat leanings of “[FLA]vour of the Weak” (1997) and “Implode” (1999). In October 1999 the band left Metropolis Records; “Epitaph”, produced by Leeb and Peterson and issued on 8 October 2001, marked its return to that label. Peterson departed after finishing work on the album, and Fulber rejoined in 2003 for “Civilization” (2004). Beyond the main discography, Leeb has led the side project Delerium since 1987, and members have worked on Noise Unit, Conjure One (Fulber), Cyberaktif (Leeb with Skinny Puppy’s cEvin Key and Dwayne Goettel) and other spin-offs. Front Line Assembly went on to release “Artificial Soldier” (2006), “Improvised Electronic Device” (2010), “Echogenetic” (2013), “Wake Up the Coma” (2019) and “Mechanical Soul” (2021), the last featuring guest appearances from Jean-Luc De Meyer of Front 242 and Dino Cazares of Fear Factory. The band caught up with Side-Line on the state of the group in 2024, with Leeb and Fulber both still in the current lineup. “Epitaph” remains the band’s eleventh studio album and, twenty-five years on, the record that reopened its relationship with Metropolis Records.

items.body: Side-Line Magazine has opened submissions for “Electronic Bodies 2,” the second volume in its electronic body music compilation series. Bands and artists making EBM and related electro-industrial styles can send in one track for consideration. The compilation will be released as a digital download via Side-Line’s Bandcamp page and promoted through Side-Line and its network of music media and DJs. The call follows “Electronic Bodies – Session 1”, Side-Line’s first EBM compilation, which brought together established names and lesser-known acts, covering old-school EBM, electro-industrial and more contemporary EBM styles. Electronic Bodies – Session 1 by Various Artists What Side-Line is looking for in ‘Electronic Bodies 2’ For this second installment, Side-Line is again looking for bands and artists making EBM, old-school industrial, electro-industrial and related electronic body music. Tracks built around pounding sequencers, aggressive basslines, mechanical rhythms or stripped-down electronic arrangements all fit the brief. New, unsigned and established acts are all welcome; selection is based on the music itself, not the size of an artist’s audience or the number of releases already out. How to submit a track for ‘Electronic Bodies 2’ Side-Line has set a few rules for submitting material, to be followed closely: Send one mastered track in WAV format, selecting the strongest material available. Submit it via WeTransfer.com to info@side-line.com; audio files sent as direct email attachments will not be accepted. Name the file using the format “Artist – Track Title.wav”. Artists must not be affiliated with GEMA, SABAM or similar collecting societies, since their licensing requirements could interfere with the compilation’s release. Artists selected for the compilation will be contacted to complete the necessary paperwork. Sending a track does not automatically guarantee inclusion; Side-Line will make a selection based on musical direction and the overall balance of the compilation. Submission deadline: November 30, 2026. The artwork accompanying this announcement is provisional and does not represent the final cover of “Electronic Bodies 2.” Side-Line will reveal the official artwork at a later stage. About the Electronic Bodies series Side-Line launched the Electronic Bodies series in January 2023, calling for submissions toward an old-school EBM compilation after a reader poll pointed the project at the early-1980s EBM sound of Belgium and its Scandinavian, Spanish and German counterparts, alongside New Beat tracks that fit the same mold. The project reached release on 1 September 2023 as “Electronic Bodies – Session 1,” an 88-track EBM charity compilation spanning EBM, New Beat and more contemporary offshoots, with all donations going to psychological support for Ukrainian soldiers and citizens affected by PTSD. Bernard Van Isacker, Side-Line’s chief editor, compiled the release and discussed the project in more detail with Side-Line ahead of its release. “Electronic Bodies 2” is the second volume in that series, with submissions open now.

items.body: Cleopatra Records will issue “Drink the New Wine”, the last studio recording by post-punk and goth rock band Bauhaus, as a 12-inch vinyl single on 30 October 2026. The pressing comes in three hand-numbered, etched color variants – white, silver and red – capped at 150 copies each, for a total of 450. Peter Murphy, Daniel Ash, David J and Kevin Haskins recorded the track separately during COVID-19 lockdown. The four traded audio files using the surrealist “exquisite corpse” method the band had used before. Bauhaus released it digitally in March 2022, its first new song since the 2008 album “Go Away White.” No Bauhaus recording has followed. Ash confirmed in April 2023 that the band’s reunion had ended, with the surviving members reforming Love and Rockets. ‘Drink the New Wine’: a lockdown recording now on hand-numbered vinyl Ash describes the track as typical of the band’s more playful side. “I always loved it when Bauhaus would go into art fart mode. Truly liberating and FUN!” he said. Cleopatra Records calls the release “a music artifact […] created for the most dedicated Bauhaus fans and collectors.” Side A of the single holds “Drink the New Wine.” Side B is etched with a reproduction of the Bauhaus logo and carries no audio. Each copy is individually hand-numbered, one color per customer, with no repressing planned once the 450 copies sell out. The single is available for pre-order through Cleopatra Records ahead of the 30 October release. About Bauhaus Small Wonder Records released Bauhaus’s debut single, “Bela Lugosi’s Dead,” in August 1979, a year after Peter Murphy, Daniel Ash, David J (David John Haskins) and his younger brother Kevin Haskins formed the band in Northampton, England. The single arrived before goth existed as a named scene. Four studio albums followed in four years on 4AD and Beggars Banquet: “In the Flat Field” (1980), “Mask” (1981), “The Sky’s Gone Out” (1982) and “Burning from the Inside” (1983). Bauhaus split on 5 July 1983, a week before “Burning from the Inside” reached shops. The pioneering band reunited for a 1998 tour and again from 2005 to 2008, a run that produced a fifth album, “Go Away White” (2008, Cooking Vinyl), released without a supporting tour. Ash, David J and Kevin Haskins had already carried their partnership into Love and Rockets, formed in 1985, and into separate solo careers. David J’s catalog includes the albums “Etiquette of Violence” and “Songs from Another Season,” plus a 2014 memoir, “Who Killed Mister Moonlight?” The four original members reunited again in 2019, announcing Peter Murphy’s first live date with Bauhaus after a heart attack ahead of shows at the Hollywood Palladium that November. A further reunion tour followed in 2022, covering Europe and the US West Coast. Months after the band released “Drink the New Wine,” Murphy’s rehab admission forced it to cancel the rest of its North American tour that August. Ash ended the reunion in April 2023, and the surviving trio returned to Love and Rockets. David J has stayed active since. He revisited his own archive on the album ‘Tracks From the Attic Revisited’ and discussed the project earlier this year in a Side-Line interview. This is the first time “Drink the New Wine” has been pressed to a physical format.

items.body: Simple Minds released their twelfth studio album, “Neon Lights”, on 8 October 2001 through Eagle Records. The Scottish post-punk and new wave band’s collection of cover versions turns 25 this year, arriving as the group’s first release after a period away from active recording. “Neon Lights” was conceived as a warm-up ahead of the following year’s “Cry” and gathers Simple Minds’ versions of songs by artists including Them, David Bowie, Pete Shelley, the Patti Smith Group, Kraftwerk, the Doors, Echo and the Bunnymen, Neil Young, Roxy Music and the Velvet Underground. Frontman Jim Kerr set out the thinking behind the project at the time of release: “Neon Lights is the first time Simple Minds have put together a collection of non-original material. We thought it was appropriate at a period of looking back that we go to the very foundations of Simple Minds, which of course is the music and the bands who influenced us.” The album followed a difficult stretch for the band. Their prior record, “Our Secrets Are the Same”, had been delivered to Chrysalis but was caught up in the label’s merger with EMI, remained unreleased, and was then leaked on the internet in 2000. Discouraged by the lost momentum, band members Eddie Duffy, Mark Taylor and Mark Kerr moved on to other projects, and Jim Kerr relocated to Sicily to work part-time as a hotelier. In 2001, Kerr and guitarist Charlie Burchill began working with multi-instrumentalist Gordon “Gordy” Goudie, a former member of the Primevals, on new material intended for “Cry”. Recorded in parallel with those sessions in Glasgow, Dublin and Taormina, Sicily, “Neon Lights” was completed and released first. Simple Minds’ ‘Neon Lights’ tracklist and credits The UK edition ran ten tracks: “Gloria” (Them), “The Man Who Sold the World” (David Bowie), “Homosapien” (Pete Shelley), “Dancing Barefoot” (Patti Smith Group), “Neon Lights” (Kraftwerk), “Hello, I Love You” (the Doors), “Bring on the Dancing Horses” (Echo and the Bunnymen), “The Needle and the Damage Done” (Neil Young), “For Your Pleasure” (Roxy Music) and “All Tomorrow’s Parties” (the Velvet Underground). A US release added two further covers, “Being Boiled” (the Human League) and “Love Will Tear Us Apart” (Joy Division). The album was produced by Jim Kerr and Charlie Burchill with Gordy Goudie, except for “Gloria”, which was produced by Phunk Investigation, Daniele Tignino and Emiliano Patrik Legato; Simon Heyworth handled mastering. Two singles followed the album: the “Dancing Barefoot” EP and a series of “Homosapien” remixes. The full album is available via Spotify. About Simple Minds Simple Minds trace back to Johnny and the Self-Abusers, a Glasgow punk band formed in early 1977 by Jim Kerr, Charlie Burchill, Tony Donald and Brian McGee. That group released a single, “Saints and Sinners”, on Chiswick Records in November 1977 and split the same day. The remaining members regrouped under the name Simple Minds, drawn from a lyric in David Bowie’s “The Jean Genie”, and played their first show on 17 January 1978 in Glasgow. Duncan Barnwell joined on second guitar that January, Mick MacNeil added keyboards in March, and Derek Forbes replaced Donald on bass in April; Barnwell left by November, leaving a settled quintet of Kerr, Burchill, MacNeil, Forbes and McGee. Manager Bruce Findlay signed the band to Zoom Records, licensed to Arista, for a 1979 debut, “Life in a Day”, which reached number 30 on the UK Albums Chart. Further albums followed in quick succession: “Real to Real Cacophony” (1979), “Empires and Dance” (1980) and the double release “Sons and Fascination” / “Sister Feelings Call” (1981). Brian McGee left after those sessions and was eventually replaced by Mel Gaynor, recruited by producer Peter Walsh in 1982 and later the band’s longest-standing drummer. Released from Arista in early 1981, Simple Minds signed to Virgin Records, and “New Gold Dream” (1982) gave the band its first Billboard 200 entry and a number 3 UK placing. “Sparkle in the Rain” (1984) debuted at number 1 in the UK and was later certified Platinum, and “Once Upon a Time” (1985) reached number 1 in the UK and the Netherlands and was certified triple Platinum in Britain, driven by the US number 1 single “Don’t You (Forget About Me)” from the film “The Breakfast Club”. Bassist Derek Forbes was dismissed in the mid-1980s and replaced by John Giblin, who debuted at Live Aid in 1985. “Street Fighting Years” (1989) topped the UK chart despite Gaynor and Giblin leaving mid-session, and keyboardist Mick MacNeil quit at the close of the subsequent tour. “Real Life” (1991) and “Good News from the Next World” (1995) followed as the band’s lineup narrowed to the core of Kerr and Burchill, with Forbes and Gaynor rejoining in 1996 and 1997 respectively. “Neapolis” (1998) was the band’s only album released through Chrysalis Records. By the time of “Neon Lights” (2001), the band had regrouped around Kerr, Burchill and new recruit Gordy Goudie, who remains in the lineup today. “Cry” followed in 2002, backed by the band’s first North American tour in seven years. Simple Minds went on to release “Black & White 050505” (2005), “Graffiti Soul” (2009), which gave the band its first UK top 10 album in 14 years, “Big Music” (2014), “Acoustic” (2016), “Walk Between Worlds” (2018) and “Direction of the Heart” (2022) through BMG. The band’s catalogue has topped 60 million albums sold worldwide, and its accolades include the 2016 Ivor Novello Award for Outstanding Song Collection and the 2014 Q Inspiration Award. The current lineup pairs founders Kerr and Burchill with Goudie, Sarah Brown, Ged Grimes, Cherisse Osei and Erik Ljunggren; in September 2026 the band announced a new studio album, “Sacrosanct”, due for release on 29 January 2027. Twenty-five years after “Neon Lights”, the covers album remains the clearest record of the influences, from Kraftwerk to Joy Division, that shaped the band’s own sound.

items.body: 2026.10.08 東京交響楽団2027/28シーズンラインナップ発表記者会見が開催！ 2年目は「危険な年」？ 2026年10月7日、ミューザ川崎シンフォニーホールで行なわれた東京交響楽団の2027／28シーズンラインナップ発表記者会見に、音楽監督ロレンツォ・ヴィオッティが登壇した。 2026／27シーズンから音楽監督に就任し、その任期が2034年3月までの延長が発表されたばかりのヴィオッティ。「まだこの第1シーズンの最中にはありますが、もうすでに楽団員はもちろんのこと、スタッフ、そして合唱団、すべての方々を私は心から誇りに思っています」と切り出した。 その実感を強くしたのが、9月に演奏したフランツ・シュミット《七つの封印の書》だった。「本当に素晴らしい演奏をしてくれました。特に合唱団は、あたかも簡単な作品であるかのように演奏してくれました。でも、実際にはもっとも難しいと言っていい作品です」。 そんな現在地から、2027／28シーズンにさらに大きな挑戦となるのが演奏会形式で上演するワーグナーの《ローエングリン》だ。「ステージのないワーグナー作品というのは、一見難しいように思われますが、《ローエングリン》は、皆さんがちょっと目をつぶって、音楽に耳を傾けていただければ、その情景の動きをありありと思い浮かべることができるオペラの一つではないかと思っています」。 シュミット作品のみならず、ヴェルディやブラームスのレクイエムを経て挑むワーグナーは、「これまで積み重ねてきた経験がすべて大きく実って、それがつながっていく作品」だと語った。 ロレンツォ・ヴィオッティ 1990年スイス・ローザンヌ出身。カダケス国際指揮者コンクール、ライプツィヒMDR指揮者コンクールなどで優勝し、2015年ザルツブルク音楽祭にてネスレ・ヤング・コンダクター賞を受賞。グルベンキアン管弦楽団首席指揮者（2018～2021）、ネーデルラント・フィルハーモニー管弦楽団およびオランダ国立歌劇場首席指揮者（2021～2025）を歴任。これまでにウィーン・フィル、ベルリン・フィル、ロイヤル・コンセルトヘボウ管、ライプツィヒ・ゲヴァントハウス管、ベルリン・シュターツカペレ、ミュンヘン・フィル、ロサンゼルス・フィル、クリーヴランド管などを指揮。オペラにおいてもウィーン国立歌劇場、パリ・オペラ座、ミラノ・スカラ座などに客演し、高い評価を得ている。 2014年、東京交響楽団との共演で日本デビュー。初共演から10年を迎えた2024年８月、東京交響楽団次期音楽監督に任命され、2026/27シーズンより第4代音楽監督に就任。2028年8月からはチューリッヒ歌劇場音楽総監督に就任する。 ©︎N.Ikegami また、音楽監督2年目にあたる来シーズンについては、「2年目こそ、ある意味での脆さが出やすい、危険性をはらんだ年になります。しかし、少しずつ相手のことがわかり始めると、当然ながら“小さなぶつかり”も出てくる。実はこれはこれで大切なことだと私は思っています」と述べた。 「私の任期も3年から8年へと延びました。長くいると、もっともっと音楽を掘り下げ、より高い質と、より多く、広く、深くということが可能になってくると思っています。これからの8年をかけて、できることすべてをする気持ちでいます。より強く、よりよい関係を築いていきたい」と力を込めた。 マーラー、ストラヴィンスキー、シューマンともっと音楽を深く掘る その関係を築いていくために、具体的にはどのようなプログラムが組まれるのか。ヴィオッティが会見で特に注目したのは、マーラー、ストラヴィンスキー、そしてシューマンだった。 今シーズンにすでに演奏したマーラーの交響曲第1番は、「新しい世界の幕開けを思わせる」作品。「本当にその、非常に音楽に対する献身と想像力、そして思い切り、すべてが求められる作品です」。そして来シーズンには交響曲第7番をとりあげる。マーラーが作曲において「和声や作曲技法において挑戦した作品と言える。技術的にも決して簡単ではない」と、オーケストラにとっても大きな挑戦になることを明かした。 そしてストラヴィンスキーについては「私の心にもっとも近い作曲家の一人で、その音色の探求を、東京交響楽団とともにできることを楽しみにしております」と期待を込めた。 最後に、シーズン終盤に置かれるのがシューマンだ。「数週間前に『今、もっとも心にある作曲家は？』と質問されて、シューマンと答えました」。ヴィオッティにとってシューマンは、重くなりすぎてもいけない。一方で、古典的に軽くなりすぎてもいけないそう。「このバランスをオーケストラとともに模索していくことが一つの課題になると思っています」。 2027年4月から3年間、ヴァイオリニストの佐藤俊介が東京交響楽団クリエイティブ・パートナーに就任することも発表されている。ヴィオッティはまだ直接会ったことはないが、オランダのオーケストラで楽団員から話を聞き、SpotifyやYouTubeなどで彼の演奏を聴いているという。 「非常に好印象を抱いています。オーケストラとしても、室内楽的に、お互いに親密によく聴き合う姿勢は、とても大事なんです。そのような意味でも彼を迎えるのは大きな意味を持つと思っています」 廣岡楽団長からは、佐藤との活動を通して、指揮者を置かずに一緒に演奏するような取り組みや、バロック音楽のアプローチ、さらにはこれまでオーケストラが取り組んでこなかったジャンルとのコラボレーションへの期待も語られた。 「声なき声のキャラクター」は米澤柊による個展である。展示作品はすべて2026年の新作で、なかでも米澤がここ一年ほど取り組んでいるという油絵作品が全体の七割近くを占めている。画面はどれも彩度の低い色が細かく重ねられることで構成されており、その茫洋とした色彩の渦を眺めるうちに、人間めいた輪郭や骨格、目、手の残像といったものたちの印象がかろうじて浮かび上がってくる。これは直感的には、白飛びした視界を思わせた。眠りから醒めたときに誰しもが味わうように、暗がりから急に光に満ちた空間へと晒された視界は明順応が間に合わず白く飽和する。そしてそこから徐々に、事物の輪郭や色彩を取り戻していく。しかし本展において、その視界が完全に明瞭になることはない。作品のあいだを行き交うにしたがい、眼球を包む涙液そのものが白濁していくかのごとく、乳白色の闇がゆるやかに立ち込める。六本木の雑居ビルの薄暗がりを切り開いてあらわれる端正なホワイトキューブともあいまって、本展はどこまでも明るく、しかし──それゆえに──知覚の不完全性を露わにしている。では、そんな淡い光の中に漂っているものたちとは一体なんなのだろうか。 ［撮影：木奥惠三］ 繰り返し述べられてきた内容のため簡潔に触れるにとどめるが、多くの手法やメディウムを横断した米澤の制作には「アニマ（魂・生命性）」への関心が通底しており、とりわけ特徴的なのが「オバケ」への着目である。「オバケ」とはアニメーション制作において、あるフレームとフレームのあいだの動きを補完し、物体の動きをより活き活きとみせるためにあえて（静止画としては）崩れた描写を行なう技術を指す。実際、現時点における米澤作品のもっとも一般的なイメージとは、身体がほどけて散らばりつつあるかのような「オバケ」としてのキャラクターたちの図像だろう。 画面内の事物を 息づかせ （ アニメートす ） るための技術が「オバケ」と呼ばれる逆説──いや、考えてみれば逆説ではないのだ。さまざまなアニメ作品において、「オバケ」のコマを単体で切り取ったスクリーンショットは作画崩壊の事例としてネットミーム化してきた。これはアニメーションの中割り技術への無知から生じた誤認にすぎないわけだが、ではなぜ人々が「オバケ」に対してそれほど強烈な印象を共有しえたのかといえば、なめらかなアニメーションのなかに「見てはいけないものを見てしまった」と感じたからにほかならないだろう。すなわち、「オバケ」とはアニメーションの物語時間を補填するために見逃され続けることを運命付けられた存在であり、それゆえ、ひとたび意識に上ったその姿は本物の怪異さながらに「ぞっとする」ものとなるのだ。 画面内におけるキャラクターの自律性が担保されるためには、無数の崩れかけた非-自律的な なにものか ・・・・・ が不可欠であるというジレンマ。米澤はこの主従──アニメーションを規定する所与の時間と、それを埋め合わせる「オバケ」という関係性──を撹乱する。ほんらい見てはいけないものである「オバケ」を一枚の図像──しかもモニタやキャンバスといったいかにも「見るべき」質感を帯びたもの──として固定したうえで、その身体の崩壊を過剰に押し進めていく。そのとき、アニメーションのなめらかさを整えるパテのごとき不定形な「オバケ」はフレームの隙間から這い出して、別の時間的秩序を育み始める──フレームレートに従って生起する単線的な物語とは異なる時間を。そこでは過去や未来は等しくまなざされ、因果もまた意味を失う。米澤はそうして、フレームとフレームのあいだの飛躍を補完するためにのみ生を許された存在に、 別種の生の可能性 （ アニマ ） を見ようとするわけだ。 このようにアニメーションをひとつの基点とする米澤の作品群は、その手法にかかわらず複雑な層性を帯びてきた。例えば米澤の代表的なシリーズである「オバケのスクリーンショット」では、現実の風景写真のなかに「オバケ」としてのキャラクターたちが描き込まれている。レイヤーの集合としてのデジタルペイントが現実の風景に重ね合わされ、しかもそれは連続する無数のフレームの一瞬を捉えた「スクリーンショット」として位置付けられる。こうした時間的・空間的な複層性のなかをたゆたう米澤の作品は、必然的に「いま・ここ」からの遊離を予感させる。イメージは確かに目の前に存在するはずなのに、どこかヴェールに包まれているような捉えどころのなさがついてまわる。それは失われたものへの憧憬なのか、来たるべきものの予兆なのか──無論、どちらでもありうる。先に述べたとおり、米澤が紡ごうとする非線形の時間的秩序のなかにおいて、過去・現在・未来は等価に立ち並んでいるのだから★1。アニマはつねに、現前と予感のあいだで見え隠れする。 この観点において、描画面をレイヤー状に切り分けるためのアナログな技術として油絵を位置付けることも可能だろう。しかし当然ながら、油絵においては絵具の乾燥状態が層を決定する。乾ききる前に次のストロークを置けば下の層は物理的に巻き込まれ、層と層の境界——それは時間的秩序そのものと言ってもいい——が相互に浸潤可能となる（もちろん、実際に米澤がそのような描法を用いたかどうかは問題ではない）。ここで層を決定しているのは描き手の意志ではなく、絵具の乾燥速度、すなわちメディウムに固有の時間である。フレームとフレームを繋ぐフラットな時間のあいだから、「オバケ」が棲まう異なる時間が這い出していったように、ここでは層と層のあいだにメディウム由来の液体的な時間感覚が流れ込んでいる★2。 ［撮影：斉藤桃加］ 本展のステートメント冒頭には「かたちを選んで描こうとするほど選ばなかったものを切りすててしまうようで息苦しく、絵は段々と白くなっていった」とある。幾重にもゆらぎながら仄かに浮かび上がる油彩のイメージは、さまざまな連想を喚起する。例えば長時間露光による写真。そこでは被写体が動くことによって輪郭がブレ、イメージは次第に発散へと向かっていく。あるいは拡散モデルにおける画像生成（を開始まもなく停止させたようす）。ここでは反対に、ブレの極点とでもいうべきノイズのなかに任意の輪郭が幻視され、イメージが浮かび上がってくる。輪郭が浮かび上がる前のさざめきと、輪郭が溶け去っていった後の残響。米澤の画面が置かれているのは、まさにその異なる二つのベクトルが調停され、判定が無化される地点／時点である。 米澤は「世界が意味になる前の複雑さについて考えたい」という。しかしここまで見てきたように「ほんらいの複雑な世界が、人間の手による記号的分節によって単純化されてしまう」という単線的な因果とは別の場所に向けてこそ、米澤の作品はひらかれているように思える。そういえば、私が米澤の油絵の画面からはじめに想起したもの。それは写真でもAIでもなく、ほとんど面影だけになってしまった記憶のことであった。限界まで薄れ抽象化された記憶は、それがどこに属するのかをもはや判別できず、ゆえに時間のあいだを自由に飛び回り、私たちの認識に影響を及ぼして回る。はじめて見たはずのものをなぜか懐かしく思うこと。反対に、何度も見たはずのものをなぜだか瑞々しく感じること。そうした認識の脱臼ともいうべき瞬間を真に受けて生き続けることが、可能であるように思えるのだ。米澤の作品世界においてならば。 ★1──個人的にここで想起するのは小林泰三「酔歩する男」である。作中では、一風変わったタイムトラベルの方法が描かれる。登場人物は「時間とは本来非連続なものであり、そこに連続性を見出しているのは私たちの脳である」との仮説を示し、実際に脳内の時間感覚を司る部位を破壊することで、さまざまな時間点をランダムに飛び回る存在となる。それは過去と未来が等しく可能性のなかに溶け込んだ非線形の人生であり、そこには始まりも終わりもありえない。 ★2──ここで思い出すのは、ジェフ・ウォールによるエッセイ「Photography and Liquid Intelligence」（1989）である。ウォールは、写真を織りなす光学と液体の緊張関係に焦点を当てた。つまりカメラという緻密な機械が生産する写真は、最終的に現像という液体の不確定性に晒されることで顕現するのであり、ウォールはここに乾いた近代的知性のオルタナティブとしての湿った知性、液体的知性を見るのである。エッセイはこの液体的知性をソラリスの海に喩えることで結ばれる。観測者の記憶からイメージを汲み出し反射させるその海には、結ばれる前のあらゆるイメージの素がたゆたいながら、こちらを見返しているわけだ。写真とは、現像液に潜む無数のイメージのひとつをたまさか拾い上げたものにすぎず、もう一度現像し直せばそこにはまったく違ったイメージが掬い取られるのかもしれない。フィルムを現像液に浸し続ければ、その還元力はやがて感光していない臭化銀にまで至り、あらゆるイメージを黒く塗りつぶしていく。それは白く飽和した油彩のイメージと対になるものだろう。 （後編へ） 鑑賞日：2026/07/25（土）
